html:
A city on a cliff over the narrows of the St. Lawrence River, founded in 1608 by the French explorer Samuel de Champlain. It was the heart of New France and is one of the oldest European cities in North America.

The name comes from an Algonquian word for "where the river narrows". From there the French traded for furs with the Huron (Wendat), Algonquin and Innu peoples and sent missionaries inland. It became the seat of the governor and of the first bishop of New France.

In 1759, during the Seven Years' War, a British army under James Wolfe climbed to the Plains of Abraham and beat the French under Montcalm outside the walls. Both generals died. The city surrendered, and in 1763 New France passed to Britain. Quebec stayed French speaking and Catholic, and is now capital of the province of Quebec. Its old walled town is a World Heritage Site.
